clue.text: Use knife to draw blood and get meat from a rib

parts.note: to use a knife on something is to cut it
to let blood is to draw it, as old physicians did

explanation.surface: A butcher's instructions: cut deep enough to bleed and you'll get a piece of rib meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlet is a small cut of meat, typically taken from the neck or ribs.

clue.text: Leave the radio playing march music?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to go out and leave the radio blaring military marches.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the answer as three words: A BAND ON, which is what the radio is when it plays march music.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to leave behind for good; split up it describes a broadcast where a band is on air.

clue.text: Uninclined to saint, but a conscientious one tries it

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Uninclined to saint, but a conscientious one tries it' gives LEVEL + ST with nothing for BE; a word (likely 'be') seems lost in OCR and no scan is available to confirm
annotationWithheld.clue: Uninclined to saint, but a conscientious one tries it

clue.text: Vessel displaying its nationality?

explanation.surface: A ship flies its national ensign for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship shows its nationality with its flag on; split up the answer says just that, while whole it is a large drinking jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or ale, a vessel in the drinking sense.

clue.text: How to make tinned monkey a tasty snack

parts.note: food that is tinned is canned, so it gives the word for a tin
an ape is a primate, loosely a monkey

explanation.surface: A mock recipe: put a monkey in a tin and you have a delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury bite served with drinks.

clue.text: Discuss the opposite point of view

explanation.surface: Talk over the view that runs counter to yours.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk together, and the converse is the reverse proposition or opposite position.

clue.text: Bill only is in deadly earnest

explanation.surface: A man named Bill is the only one who is truly serious.
explanation.walkthrough: A parliamentary bill is not yet an act, so a bill alone is 'no act'; the same phrase means not pretending.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill becomes law only when passed, so a mere bill is no Act; someone sincere is putting on no act.

clue.text: In house of chastity sex appeal gets preference

indicators.note: the sex appeal sits in the religious house, placed inside its letters

parts.note: a priory is a monastery or convent whose members take vows of chastity
IT is old slang for sex appeal, from the 1920s 'It girl'

explanation.surface: Inside a convent, attractiveness is given special favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Priority means precedence, the state of being given first preference.

clue.text: It is used up whenever it's needed

definitions.text: It is used up whenever it's needed

parts.words: It is used up whenever it's needed
parts.note: not consumed but put up, opened over your head each time rain falls

explanation.surface: Something runs out every time you need it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used up' suggests consumed; the object is in fact raised up over the head whenever it rains.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain shade is put up whenever there is a shower.

clue.text: Formally dressed to take up occupation

explanation.surface: Someone puts on formal clothes before moving into a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN HABIT, the first half means wearing a habit, formal or religious dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit is to occupy or dwell in a place; in a habit means clothed in a riding or monk's garment.

clue.text: Clean cut it makes

indicators.note: the word clean is cut up and its letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: A surgeon's tool makes a neat incision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' signals an anagram of CLEAN, and the whole clue also describes the answer, a blade that makes a clean cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance or lancet is a sharp blade for piercing or cutting, as in lancing a boil.

clue.text: Tender Conservative makes charitable collection

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as with a bid
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted Tory organises a fundraising collection.
explanation.definitionFit: An offertory is the collection of money taken at a church service.

clue.text: Boarded with iron and old copper

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a copper coin, the old British penny, was abbreviated d

explanation.surface: A ship's hull is reinforced with iron and ancient copper sheeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To be boarded is to be given meals as a lodger, that is, fed.

clue.text: Brass used extensively for note-making

parts.note: a brass instrument extended by its slide to produce musical notes, not a pen

explanation.surface: Senior officers spend a lot of time writing memos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like top officials and 'note-making' like writing; the extension is the instrument's slide.
explanation.definitionFit: This slide instrument is in the brass section and its slide is pushed out to lower the notes.

clue.text: Sort of betting convention evokes little spirit

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds used in off-course betting
a rite is a customary ceremony or convention

explanation.surface: A gambling custom calls up a small ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the British bookmakers' term for the odds at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a fairy or elf, a small supernatural being.

clue.text: One who saves little money is likely to save little money

definitions.text: One who saves little money is likely to save little money

parts.words: One who saves little money is likely to save little money
parts.note: careful with small coins, and so likely to accumulate only a small sum overall

explanation.surface: A careful saver of small sums will end up with little to show.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'penny-wise and pound-foolish': saving coppers while wasting large sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful over trivial amounts while careless with large ones keeps total savings small.

clue.text: Weapons never used at the front?

explanation.surface: Some weapons are never deployed on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidearms are carried at the side, so playfully they are never used at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and swords worn at the belt are weapons carried at one's side rather than in front.

clue.text: South Pennsylvania resort

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A holiday town in the southern part of an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town with mineral springs where people go to take the waters.

clue.text: Literary fastidiousness of editor entering food store

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, sitting within its letters

parts.note: a pantry is a cupboard or room for storing food

explanation.surface: A fussy editor slips into the larder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with minor details and formal rules of learning.

clue.text: River crossed by Dum?

explanation.surface: A river that someone called Dum has to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll, Tweedledum and Tweedledee quarrel; Dum is crossed by his twin, who completes the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales; Tweedledee is the twin who crossed Tweedledum.

clue.text: Very little time

explanation.surface: Hardly any time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute means tiny, and a minute is sixty seconds.

clue.text: Pickled roe is an output of mine

indicators.note: something pickled is preserved and altered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Preserved fish eggs are among what the mine produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is rock containing metal, extracted from a mine.

clue.text: Japanese money invested in source of sugar and spice

indicators.note: the currency is put inside, as money is invested in a venture

parts.note: sugar cane is a source of sugar
the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: Japanese cash is put into sugar and spice businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper spice.

clue.text: Gunner is instrumental in discovering water line

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners
taken as written
a band is an instrumental music group

explanation.surface: An artillery soldier helps find a waterline.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British Army's gunnery regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainband is a dark band in the solar spectrum caused by water vapour in the air.

clue.text: A party Communist much loved

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
red is a common term for a Communist

explanation.surface: A Communist at a party is greatly adored.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means loved deeply.

clue.text: Public protest puts editor back out of fashion

parts.note: a demo is a public demonstration or protest

indicators.note: the editor piece is turned around and read backwards

explanation.surface: A protest makes an editor return to unfashionable ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Démodé is French-derived for outmoded, no longer in style.

clue.text: Fed up about stewed pear being divided

indicators.note: the full-up word goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: fed up here means full, sated

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked down, so the letters of pear are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone sick of stewed pears is coming apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' tempts as weary or annoyed; here it means filled with food, full. 'stewed' scrambles the pear, and 'about' wraps the full-up word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Separated means divided or set apart.

clue.text: Fossil deposit found in Camber ley

indicators.note: the letters sit within the town name, found inside it

explanation.surface: Fossils turned up in the Surrey town of Camberley.
explanation.walkthrough: Camberley is a town in Surrey, England; the page splits the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is fossilised tree resin.

clue.text: What a captain takes to the West when the seas rage

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west
a captain takes the helm, the steering wheel or tiller

explanation.surface: A captain steers west through a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelm is to engulf or submerge, what raging seas do to ships.

clue.text: In favour of a bet placed as proof of will power

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: a bet placed is laid down, and the letters of a bet are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes money to show determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Probate is the legal proof that a will is valid, giving executors their authority.

clue.text: Weathered the oceans I'd add

parts.note: the seas are the oceans
I is the numeral one and the 'd of I'd is D

explanation.surface: A sailor says the oceans should be included.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned timber or people have been weathered and toughened by exposure.

clue.text: Bird which hunts outsize victims

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
prey are the victims of a hunter

explanation.surface: A bird that hunts creatures larger than itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey.
